questions.q: Which of these is a real example of a publicly-exposed storage misconfiguration CSPM catches?
options: An S3 bucket or Azure Storage account set to allow public read access
A storage account using the default region
A bucket with versioning enabled
A storage account tagged for cost tracking
questions.explain: The classic finding is a storage resource left with public read access enabled, often from a quick file-sharing task.

questions.q: What does a security group rule of 0.0.0.0/0 on port 22 mean?
options: SSH access is open to the entire internet
Only internal traffic can reach the resource
The port is completely closed
It only affects IPv6 traffic
questions.explain: 0.0.0.0/0 means any IPv4 address, so that rule opens SSH (port 22) to anyone on the internet, not just the organization's network.

questions.q: Why is an IAM policy with "Action": "*" and "Resource": "*" considered a misconfiguration?
options: It grants far more permission than almost any job actually needs
It is required for all IAM policies to function
It only applies to read-only operations
It automatically expires after 24 hours
questions.explain: A wildcard Action and Resource grants every possible action on every possible resource -- excessive permission CSPM flags as a finding.

questions.q: What encryption-related issue does CSPM commonly flag?
options: Encryption at rest disabled or set weaker than the required baseline
Encryption keys rotating too frequently
Too many encryption algorithms enabled at once
Encryption applied to non-sensitive test data
questions.explain: Even though most providers offer encryption at rest by default, CSPM flags resources where it's disabled or weaker than the baseline requires.

questions.q: Why does CSPM flag privileged accounts without MFA enforced?
options: Because a privileged account reachable with a password alone is a high-value target for attackers
Because MFA is only relevant for customer-facing accounts
Because passwords are inherently more secure than MFA
Because MFA is required only in Europe
questions.explain: Privileged accounts are exactly what an attacker wants to compromise first, so a missing MFA requirement is a serious finding.
